h1:
Nakhon Phanom–Sakon Nakhon
3 Days of Temples and Nature
intro: Nakhon Phanom and Sakon Nakhon are neighbours, only about 90-something kilometres apart along Highway 22, so plenty of people who make it to Nakhon Phanom decide to tack Sakon Nakhon onto the same trip. The two pair up really well, because Nakhon Phanom is all about its Mekong-side stupas and river views, while Sakon Nakhon has Phra That Choeng Chum, the city's own stupa, forest-tradition temples like Wat Pa Sutthawat, plus nature up in the Phu Phan hills such as Wat Tham Pha Daen and Nong Han lake. This trip runs over 3 days: Nakhon Phanom first, then across to Sakon Nakhon, covering both the temple side and the nature side, with real timings, distances and eateries that are actually open. Updated for 2026.

blocks.html: If you're already flying or driving into Nakhon Phanom, carrying on to Sakon Nakhon is a smart use of time, since the two towns sit on the same Highway 22. It's about 93 km from downtown Nakhon Phanom to downtown Sakon Nakhon, roughly an hour and a half. Along the way you pass Ban Tha Rae, the largest Catholic village in Thailand, which makes a natural stop just before you reach Sakon Nakhon town. So the drive isn't just shifting between towns; there's a worthwhile stop along the way too.

This plan keeps Nakhon Phanom for the first day at an unhurried pace, focusing on Phra That Phanom and the riverfront in town. Day two you cross over to Sakon Nakhon for the city's main stupa and a forest-tradition temple, and day three is a nature day up in the Phu Phan hills before looping back. Every location and distance is measured from each province's town centre so your timings stay accurate. If you only have 2 days, drop day three, or fold the Phu Phan leg into day two if you start early.

blocks.text: Why pair Nakhon Phanom with Sakon Nakhon

blocks.html: The main reasons are the short distance and the fact that the two towns have characters that complement rather than repeat each other. Here's what each one gives you.

items.name: Nakhon Phanom — Mekong stupas
items.blurb: Known for its Mekong River views and Phra That Phanom, the principal stupa of the upper Isan region. The town has an easy riverside promenade, a Vietnamese clock tower, and good Vietnamese food from the old community. A nice way to open the trip with a riverside mood.

items.name: Sakon Nakhon — temples & Phu Phan
items.blurb: Home to Phra That Choeng Chum, the city's own stupa, Wat Pa Sutthawat with its relics and Luang Pu Mun museum, plus nature up in the Phu Phan hills like Wat Tham Pha Daen and Nong Han, a large freshwater lake. A good way to close the trip with a mix of merit-making and nature.

items.name: Connecting road — Highway 22
items.blurb: About 93 km links the two towns, roughly an hour and a half. The road is good and traffic is light, passing the Catholic village of Ban Tha Rae before Sakon Nakhon, so the drive has a stop to break it up and never gets dull.

blocks.title: Which direction drives best
blocks.html: If you're using your own car or a rental, do Nakhon Phanom first because the airport is in Nakhon Phanom; finish in Sakon Nakhon, then loop back to Nakhon Phanom to fly out. Or if you've driven in yourself, you can end the trip in Sakon Nakhon and head straight back toward Udon Thani. Highway 22 runs on to Udon, so there's no need to double back.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Nakhon Phanom: Phra That Phanom and the Mekong

blocks.html: Day one stays entirely on the Nakhon Phanom side. In the morning head south to pay respects at the main Phra That Phanom; in the afternoon loop back into town to walk the riverfront and see the key spots; in the evening catch the sunset over the water. It's a day that combines merit-making with an easygoing riverside-town atmosphere.

items.activity: Leave downtown Nakhon Phanom and drive south along the riverside road to That Phanom district
items.note: About 50 km, roughly 1 hour, with Mekong views the whole way

items.activity: Pay respects at Phra That Phanom, the principal stupa on the Mekong
items.note: A white gold-topped chedi about 53 metres tall; walk the clockwise circuit. Free entry, dress modestly, remove shoes before stepping onto the terrace

items.activity: Stroll the market in front of the temple and pick up local souvenirs
items.note: Local sweets and Isan souvenirs to choose from, and the area in front of the temple photographs well

items.activity: Lunch on Mekong fish at Khrua Rim Khong View, That Phanom
items.note: A riverside spot about 2 km from the stupa, open 9.00 am–8.30 pm, known for big plates of fried fish at reasonable prices

items.activity: Drive back into Nakhon Phanom town, walk the riverfront and Phaya Sri Sattanakkharat
items.note: The brass naga figure on the riverbank is a signature check-in spot for the town, with good angles from every side

items.activity: See the Vietnamese Memorial Clock Tower and the old town quarter
items.note: This quarter has old buildings and long-running Vietnamese restaurants, easy for an evening stroll

items.activity: Catch the sunset from the riverfront, then find dinner in town
items.note: The riverfront is breezy and pleasant in the evening, with restaurants and a weekend walking street

blocks.title: Want to add more Nakhon Phanom stupas
blocks.html: If you're specifically into the birthday-of-the-week stupas, Nakhon Phanom has all seven spread across its districts. On this first day you could slot in Phra That Renu Nakhon (Monday) on the same road near That Phanom. But if you're crossing to Sakon Nakhon on day two as this plan does, it's better to stick to just the main one so your timings don't blow out.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Across to Sakon Nakhon: Phra That Choeng Chum and Ban Tha Rae

blocks.html: Day two is the crossing-over day. Leave Nakhon Phanom in the morning and drive along Highway 22 toward Sakon Nakhon, stopping at Ban Tha Rae to see the Catholic village and its ship-shaped cathedral, then into Sakon Nakhon town to pay respects at Phra That Choeng Chum and to honour Luang Pu Mun at Wat Pa Sutthawat. It's a culture-and-merit day that shows you several sides of Sakon Nakhon.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Across to Sakon Nakhon: Choeng Chum–Tha Rae

items.activity: Leave downtown Nakhon Phanom and drive Highway 22 toward Sakon Nakhon
items.note: About 93 km, roughly an hour and a half, good road with no traffic

items.activity: Stop at Ban Tha Rae to see St. Michael the Archangel Cathedral
items.note: The largest Catholic village in Thailand, founded in 1884; the ship-shaped cathedral references the community's migration. About 21 km from Sakon Nakhon town

items.activity: Walk among the colonial-era buildings in the Tha Rae community
items.note: Century-old houses with a European-meets-Vietnamese feel; there's the old-style Francisco khao piak shop in a vintage house to stop and eat at

items.activity: Enter Sakon Nakhon town and pay respects at Phra That Choeng Chum, Wat Phra That Choeng Chum Worawihan
items.note: Sakon Nakhon's city stupa; pay respects to Luang Pho Ong Saen, the temple's revered Buddha image. Dress modestly

items.activity: Lunch in Sakon Nakhon town, then on to Wat Pa Sutthawat
items.note: Wat Pa Sutthawat is within the town; it's where Luang Pu Mun Bhuridatto was cremated

items.activity: Visit the Luang Pu Mun museum at Wat Pa Sutthawat
items.note: It has a wax figure of Luang Pu Mun and his actual belongings; a calm setting well suited to quiet meditation

items.activity: Check into your accommodation in Sakon Nakhon, rest and find dinner
items.note: Sakon Nakhon town has local-food restaurants and an evening market to wander

blocks.title: Ban Tha Rae and special dates
blocks.html: Ban Tha Rae is especially lively during the Christmas Star Procession festival in late December, when villagers make decorative stars for the parade across the whole village. Come then and you'll catch an atmosphere that's hard to see otherwise, but it's crowded and rooms fill up fast, so book ahead. On an ordinary weekday you can wander the village and take photos at ease without booking anything.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Phu Phan nature: Wat Tham Pha Daen and Nong Han

blocks.html: The last day switches to nature up in the Phu Phan hills. In the morning head up to Wat Tham Pha Daen, with its cliff-face carvings and large naga-hooded image, plus views of Sakon Nakhon town from the hill. In the afternoon come down to Nong Han, Isan's large freshwater lake, before looping back. It's a day of both high views and water views to close the trip on an easy note.

items.activity: Leave downtown Sakon Nakhon and drive up into the Phu Phan hills to Wat Tham Pha Daen
items.note: In Dong Mafai subdistrict, about 17 km from town; the final stretch is an uphill climb, so take the curves carefully

items.activity: See Wat Tham Pha Daen, the cliff-face carvings and the naga-hooded image
items.note: The carvings on the rock face depict scenes from the Buddha's life, and there's a viewpoint over Sakon Nakhon town from the hill

items.activity: Walk the photo spots and pause for coffee at a Phu Phan view café on the way down
items.note: The way down has cafés and viewpoints to stop at, and the hilltop air is cool and pleasant in the morning

items.activity: Head back down to town for a lunch of local Sakon Nakhon food
items.note: Try mu tap wan (sweet pork liver) or local Isan dishes at a restaurant in town

items.activity: Go to Nong Han, the large freshwater lake on the edge of Sakon Nakhon town
items.note: Stroll along Nong Han or take a boat for the views; there's a public park and a sunset spot

items.activity: Catch Nong Han in the evening light, then head home
items.note: If you're flying out of Nakhon Phanom, drive back on Highway 22, about an hour and a half. If you drove yourself, you can carry straight on to Udon Thani

blocks.title: Allow time for the climb up Phu Phan
blocks.html: The final stretch up to Wat Tham Pha Daen is a narrow, steep hill road. In a sedan, use a low gear and drive slowly. During the rainy season the road can get slippery, so go in the morning while the sun is still gentle and the road is dry. If you'd rather not drive yourself, there are songthaews and guided tours from town that can take you up; ask your accommodation or TAT Sakon Nakhon ahead of time.

blocks.text: Add these if you have more time in Sakon Nakhon

blocks.html: If you stretch the trip to 4 days or want to go deeper into Sakon Nakhon, there are several more merit and nature spots you can add depending on your interests.

items: Phu Phan Ratchanivet Palace — a royal residence set in the Phu Phan forest, open to visitors only when there is no royal stay; check the opening schedule before you go. The grounds and atmosphere are shaded and cool.

Ajahn Fan Ajaro Museum — at Wat Pa Udom Somphon in Phanna Nikhom district, a lotus-petal-shaped chedi holding the relics and belongings of Ajahn Fan; forest-tradition followers often go here after Wat Pa Sutthawat.
Phu Pha Yon / Phu Phan National Park — hiking trails and waterfalls in the Phu Phan hills, good for a full nature day. Bring hiking shoes and ask about trail conditions beforehand.
Sakon Nakhon indigo and natural-dye cloth — Sakon Nakhon is famous for hand-dyed indigo cloth, with weaving communities and shops where you can buy it as a souvenir you'll only find locally.

blocks.text: What to eat across the two provinces

blocks.html: The Nakhon Phanom–Sakon Nakhon route has two styles of food to try. The Nakhon Phanom side is strong on Mekong fish and Vietnamese food, while the Sakon Nakhon side is strong on local Isan dishes and the eats in the Tha Rae community. Here are places that are actually open and that locals go to.

items: Khrua Rim Khong View, That Phanom — a riverside Mekong-fish spot about 2 km from Phra That Phanom, open 9.00 am–8.30 pm. Big plates of fried fish at reasonable prices, good for lunch on day one.
Vietnamese food in Nakhon Phanom town — the town has long-running Vietnamese restaurants from the old community; naem nueang, mu yo and khao piak are the must-tries. Good for dinner on day one.

Francisco old-style khao piak, Ban Tha Rae — a shop in a century-old colonial house in the middle of the Tha Rae community, known for its local-style khao piak noodles. A good late-morning stop while crossing between provinces.

Local food in Sakon Nakhon town — Sakon Nakhon town has Isan restaurants and the well-known mu tap wan (sweet pork liver), found in town. Good for lunch on day three, before or after coming down from Phu Phan.

blocks.text: Getting around and what to prepare

items: Rent a car / drive yourself — the best way to control your timing for a cross-province trip like this, since the sights are spread out and some are outside town. Highway 22 is an easy drive on a good road.
Intercity buses — buses and vans run between Nakhon Phanom and Sakon Nakhon every day, good if you don't drive, but in the destination town you'll need to catch a songthaew or hire a ride.
Fly into Nakhon Phanom — the airport is in Nakhon Phanom with daily flights from Bangkok; renting a car on arrival is convenient, which fits opening the trip in Nakhon Phanom as this plan does.
Carry cash and offerings — flowers, incense and candles can be bought in front of the temples, but many places still don't take transfers, so keep cash and drinking water in the car.
Dress modestly at temples — at Phra That Phanom, Phra That Choeng Chum and Wat Tham Pha Daen, no tank tops or shorts above the knee, and remove shoes before stepping onto the stupa terrace.

faq.q: How far is Nakhon Phanom to Sakon Nakhon, and how long does it take?
faq.a: Downtown Nakhon Phanom to downtown Sakon Nakhon is about 93 km along Highway 22, roughly an hour and a half by car on a good road with light traffic. Along the way you pass Ban Tha Rae, the Catholic village about 21 km before Sakon Nakhon town, which makes a perfect stop.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Nakhon Phanom–Sakon Nakhon?
faq.a: Three days is comfortable. Day one in Nakhon Phanom for Phra That Phanom and the Mekong, day two across to Sakon Nakhon for Phra That Choeng Chum with a stop at Ban Tha Rae, and day three a nature day in the Phu Phan hills at Wat Tham Pha Daen and Nong Han. If you only have 2 days, drop day three or fold the Phu Phan leg into day two by starting early.

faq.q: How is Phra That Choeng Chum in Sakon Nakhon different from Phra That Phanom in Nakhon Phanom?
faq.a: Phra That Phanom in Nakhon Phanom is the principal stupa on the Mekong, a white gold-topped chedi about 53 metres tall. Phra That Choeng Chum in Sakon Nakhon is the city stupa within the town, and the temple has Luang Pho Ong Saen, its revered Buddha image, to pay respects to. Both are deeply respected by locals, and you can visit them both in one trip.

faq.q: Can you drive a sedan up to Wat Tham Pha Daen?
faq.a: Yes, but the final stretch is a narrow, steep hill road, so use a low gear and drive slowly. In the rainy season the road can get slippery, so it's better to go in the morning when it's dry. If you're not confident, there are songthaews and guided tours from town that can take you up; ask your accommodation or TAT Sakon Nakhon ahead of time.

faq.q: What is there to see at Ban Tha Rae?
faq.a: Ban Tha Rae is the largest Catholic village in Thailand, founded back in 1884. The highlight is St. Michael the Archangel Cathedral, designed in the shape of a ship, along with colonial-era buildings with a European-meets-Vietnamese feel. There's an old-style khao piak shop in a vintage house to stop and eat at, and it gets especially lively during the Christmas Star Procession in late December.
